title: The Exit Interview
logline: The gang's dermatologist retires, and the only one in the city with openings is Stella Zinman, so Ted's ex-fiancée starts seeing each of his friends in a paper gown. Ted is sure she's finally conducting the exit interview she never gave him, while Lily, Marshall and Robin become her most devoted patients and Barney discovers she has been booked, for him specifically, every weekday since 2008.
coldOpen: Kids, in the spring of 2013, every one of my friends started seeing my ex-fiancée behind my back. Professionally. She was a dermatologist. It was still a betrayal.

couch.line: Stella? The lady from the movie Grandma makes us watch at Thanksgiving?
Grandma thinks it's a comedy, Penny.

guests.name: Rhonda Pettibone
guests.role: Dr. Zinman's receptionist for twenty years across two states; recognizes every patient by their hands, guards the appointment book like a bank vault, has never once been impressed, and took the shrimp home from Ted's wedding

scenes.summary: Lily announces the gang's new dermatologist: Stella Zinman, new in Midtown and the only one with openings. Lily is already a convert, Marshall and Robin are booked. Ted's theory: Stella never gave him an exit interview, so she's conducting one now, through his friends in paper gowns. Barney is outraged to be the only one not invited, calls, and is told her next opening is never. Button: Ted thinks she's surrounding him; Robin points out that's what skin does.

beats.line: That spring, our dermatologist of ten years retired to Florida. He got a sunburn at the airport.
Good news. I found us a new dermatologist. In network, taking patients, and she is incredible.
Who?
Ted, before I say it, remember that you're a professor. You wear elbow patches. You're very mature.
Why would I need my elbow patches to—
Stella Zinman.
Stella? The Stella who left me in front of two hundred guests and a string quartet?
The quartet was great, though. They played through the whole thing. Very professional.
She just opened a practice in Midtown. She has openings because she's new. Not because she's bad.
She looked at me for ninety seconds and said, your skin is perfect, and your bangs are a cry for help.
And that's good?
It's the most honest anyone has ever been with me! I tried to tip her!
I'm Thursday. Robin's right after me. She does the full-body check.
Full body? My ex-fiancée is going to see you naked?
In a paper gown, Ted. It's medical. And it's been years since anyone looked at my back with real interest.
Everyone at the station tells me I look great. I want one opinion from somebody who isn't wearing makeup.
Don't you see what's happening? Stella left me with no explanation. No closing statement. No exit interview.
Ted, it's been five years. Normal people move on. Or get bangs.
She's doing it now. Through them. She gets you in a paper gown, cold, vulnerable, and she says...
So. How's Ted?
I do get chatty when I'm cold.
Promise me. Every question she asks about me, you remember it word for word.
Wait. A hot blonde doctor is seeing every one of you in a paper gown. And I'm the only one not invited?
It's a skin check, Barney. It's not a party.
Lily. Anything with a gown is a party.
Hello. I'd like an appointment with Dr. Zinman. The name is Stinson. Barney Stinson.
Her next opening is never? Great. Is that a Tuesday?
She hung up. Ted, do you know how long it's been since a woman told me never?
Tuesday.
You see? She's isolating Barney. Three of my friends in one week. She's surrounding me.
She's a dermatologist, Ted. Surrounding people is what skin does.

scenes.summary: Stella's new waiting room. Ted has come along 'for moral support' with Modern Bride. Rhonda, Stella's receptionist, took the shrimp home from Ted's wedding. Stella is brisk: Ted's friends are her best referrals, don't make it weird; she has no time for intrigue. Ted's imagined interrogation is contradicted by Marshall, who loved it and was asked nothing. Barney tries to book as Ted Mosby; Rhonda reveals Stella's standing appointment: every weekday at 4:15, not seeing Barney, since the week after the wedding. Robin comes out a convert. Nobody was asked about Ted, which he finds suspicious. Button: Rhonda's only question about Ted is whether he's keeping the magazine.

beats.line: That Thursday, I went with Marshall to his appointment. Purely for moral support.
Remember. Anything she asks about me. Word for word.
Ted, I'm nervous enough. The last doctor who looked at my back just said, huh.
You're Ted Mosby.
Have we met?
Your wedding. Table nine. I took the shrimp home. Somebody had to.
Ms. Scherbatsky. Gun range calluses. Scotch on the left thumb. Welcome.
She gets me.
Marshall Eriksen?
Ted.
Stella.
Do you have an appointment?
Moral support.
For a skin check.
I'm very sensitive.
Ted, your friends are my best referrals. Lily alone has sent me eleven kindergarten parents and a lunch lady. Don't make this weird.
I'm not making it weird.
You're reading Modern Bride.
It was on top!
What are you really doing with my friends, Stella?
Ted, I commute from New Jersey and I have a nine-year-old. I don't have time for intrigue. I eat lunch in the Lincoln Tunnel.
Marshall. Let's go. You get eleven minutes, and four of them are me washing my hands.
Kids, I knew exactly what was happening in that room.
Lovely skin, Mr. Eriksen. Be a shame if something happened to it.
I'll never talk.
Then I'll have to check between your toes.
He sleeps with a night-light shaped like the Chrysler Building!
Get all that?
Chrysler. Building.
Ted. That was the best four minutes of my life.
What did she ask about me?
Nothing. She doesn't do small talk. I was still saying hello when she said goodbye.
The spot on my shoulder I've been worried about since 2009? She said, that's a freckle, Marshall. You can stop naming it.
You named it?
Tarkenton.
Ms. Scherbatsky. Go on back. Leave the scotch thumb out here.
Good afternoon. Ted Mosby. I'm here for my appointment.
Ted Mosby is in seat one.
Different Ted Mosby. Very common name. Ask any architect.
Mr. Stinson.
How did you—
Your hands. You moisturize three times a day, and you have never once washed a dish.
Fine. Barney Stinson. Next available.
Dr. Zinman is booked. For you, specifically. Forever.
Every weekday at four fifteen, she blocks out fifteen minutes to not see you.
beats.title: Dr. Zinman, standing appointment

beats.line: She blocks out time for me every single day. That's the most commitment a woman has ever shown me.
She's had it since the week after your wedding, Mr. Mosby.
Barney. What did you do?
Nothing! Nothing traceable.
Ted. She said I look exactly my age.
I work in television, Ted. Nobody has ever said that to me. I almost proposed.
And me? Did she ask about me?
No.
Five years. Three of my best friends in paper gowns. Zero questions. That's the most suspicious number of questions there is.
Or it's the normal number of questions people ask about you.
I have a question about you, Mr. Mosby.
Yes?
Are you keeping the Modern Bride?

scenes.summary: Sunday brunch at Cafe Lorraine, a month later. Every friend except Barney is now Stella's patient, and they've caught her bluntness: Lily, Marshall and Robin are devastatingly honest with Ted, out of care. Ted rants that she never mentions him. Lily cracks: Stella asked one question, whether Ted ever came back for session ten of his tattoo removal. The butterfly is nine-tenths gone; Lily declares it a moth. Ted realizes he's not a mystery, he's an open chart, and decides to go back for session ten and his exit interview. Barney, who has tried everything (even Ranjit got in), insists on coming. Button: Marshall says goodbye to the moth.

beats.line: Within a month, all my friends were Stella's patients. And at Sunday brunch, I noticed something had happened to them.
So. New haircut. Thoughts?
Honestly? It looks like your head lost a custody battle.
Lily!
Dr. Zinman says honesty is a form of care. And I care about you so much, Ted.
I care about you too, buddy. Your boots click. Everyone on the subway hates you.
And your toast is going to be too long.
What toast?
The one you're about to give. I can see it in your shoulders.
You know what's worse than all of you being honest? All of you being honest without me.
This is exactly what she wants. She's turning you against me. One honest sentence at a time.
Ted, she never even mentions you.
Fifteen appointments! Not one mention! Do you know how hard it is not to mention me? I'm extremely mentionable!
Lilypad. You're doing your secret face.
I don't have a secret face.
Lily, your face is sweating a confession.
Okay! She asked one question! At my follow-up! One!
I knew it! What did she ask?
She asked if you ever came back for session ten.
Oh.
Session ten of what?
Nothing.
Laser removal. Of Ted's tattoo.
Ted Mosby has a tattoo?
Had. Mostly had. Nine-tenths had.
Wait. Dad has a tattoo?
Had, Penny. A small, tasteful butterfly. On the lower back. We will never speak of it again.
So there's one-tenth of a butterfly back there?
Just one little wing.
It's a moth now.
After the wedding, going back for the last session felt weird. So I just didn't.
That's all she wants. Not intel. Five years, and I'm not a mystery that haunts her. I'm an open chart.
Ted, honestly? Five years later, the only thing she wants from you is to finish removing you.
Then I'm going back. Session ten. And this time, I'm getting my exit interview.
And I'm coming with you.
Why?
Ted, I've tried everything. Flowers. A lawyer. A second lawyer to sue the first lawyer.
I sent Ranjit in with a fake rash.
And?
Ranjit got in. Ranjit loves her. Ranjit has a skincare routine now.
Fine. But we're in and out. She closes her chart, I get my answers, nobody gets weird.
Five bucks says he comes out engaged.
Goodbye, moth.

scenes.summary: Friday, 4:14 p.m. Session ten is done: the butterfly is extinct and Stella's chart is finally closed. Ted asks for his exit interview; Stella gives it like a performance review (strengths: Lucy, handwriting, would move to New Jersey; areas for improvement: wedding chairs labeled by personality). Then the real talk: he did nothing wrong, she knew in the car, she's sorry for the timing, not the leaving; they'd have been fine, and he deserved more than fine. Her verdict: you were always fine, just never mine. Undercut: she still hasn't seen Star Wars. At 4:15 Barney bursts in for his standing appointment with a pineapple; the reason he's banned is the congratulations fruit basket he sent her the day after the wedding. Her verdict on Barney: completely average. He books the same time Monday. Future Ted: it's still running.

beats.line: So that Friday, at 4:04 in the afternoon, I went back for session ten. It took four minutes. I'd been avoiding it for five years.
There. The butterfly is officially extinct.
Chart closed. Five years late.
Rhonda, do you know how good that feels? He was nine-tenths of my best work. It kept me up at night.
Can I ask you something? Not as a patient.
Rhonda, give us a minute.
I'll be at the coffee machine. Hearing everything.
You never gave me an exit interview. You left, and I never found out what I did wrong.
You want an exit interview? Fine. Strengths. Wonderful with Lucy. Beautiful handwriting. Willing to move to New Jersey, which nobody is.
Areas for improvement. You labeled our wedding chairs by personality.
It was a seating chart with a narrative arc!
Ted. You didn't do anything wrong. I knew in the car on the way there. I should have known a month before.
That part, I'm sorry for.
Just that part?
Just that part. Not the leaving. You were going to build me a reading nook in the shape of my initial.
It was a Z. It was a great nook.
We'd have been fine, Ted. Fifty years of fine. And you're a man who's supposed to be ridiculous about somebody.
So. Doctor. Honest verdict.
You're fine, Ted. You were always fine. You were just never mine.
Also, I still haven't seen Star Wars.
Stella! It's been five years!
Best five years of my life.
Four fifteen! I'm here for my standing appointment!
Your appointment is that she doesn't see you.
And yet, here we are. Seeing each other.
I'm looking at Ted.
I brought a pineapple. The universal symbol of welcome. Stella, why won't you see me?
The day after the wedding, a fruit basket came to my house.
Lots of people send fruit.
The card said, congratulations on dodging Mosby. Call me.
Barney!
It was a very nice basket, Ted! It had a pineapple!
So I blocked out fifteen minutes a day to never see you. Second-best decision I made that week.
What was the first?
Right.
Fine. But you can see me from there. Give it to me straight, Doctor. The verdict.
Your skin is completely average.
Average?
The hands said average too.
Same time Monday?
I'll be not seeing you.
It's a date.
Kids, that appointment is twenty-two years old now. It's the longest relationship your Uncle Barney's ever had.
